scenes.headline: How a splat's colour changes with your viewpoint
scenes.sub: Spherical harmonics, sharp lobes, and a tiny shared network
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Glint! A Gaussian splat looks different from every angle. Here is how that colour is stored, and a much smaller way.

scenes.text: Keep eight numbers per Gaussian, and let one tiny network shared by the whole scene turn them into view-dependent colour.
scenes.mark: one tiny network shared by the whole scene
scenes.say: The idea: keep eight numbers per Gaussian, and let one tiny network, shared by the whole scene, turn them into colour that changes with the view.

scenes.title: Every model has the same shape
scenes.say: Every appearance model in this comparison has the same shape.

parts.say: A base colour, the same from every angle.

parts.note: the shift for view direction d
parts.say: A residual that depends on the view direction. Only this part changes between models.

parts.note: keeps the result a valid colour
parts.say: And an activation that keeps the result a valid colour.

scenes.title: Two ways to bend the colour

left.title: Spherical harmonics
left.say: Spherical harmonics store forty-five weights per Gaussian on a fixed basis. Cheap to evaluate, but only smooth bumps.

right.title: One stretched lobe
right.say: A lobe model stores one sharp, stretched highlight that can point anywhere. Eight numbers, far fewer bytes.

steps.say: Start with the direction from camera to Gaussian, written as spherical harmonic values, computed on the fly.
Each Gaussian keeps just eight learned features.
One tiny network, shared by the whole scene, reads both, right inside the rasterizer.
Its output is a small colour shift, added to the base colour.

scenes.title: Appearance bytes per Gaussian
scenes.say: That is twenty-eight bytes per Gaussian, against a hundred and ninety-two for spherical harmonics, and faster training.

steps.say: Here is the garden scene from above.
Render only the view-dependent part, and a ring appears in the grass, where the camera operator stepped during capture.

scenes.text: Expressive colour models keep reflections out of the geometry, but they also learn whatever changed during the capture.
scenes.say: Expressive colour keeps reflections out of the geometry. But it also learns whatever changed while you were filming.
